summary.text: A 24-year-old woman with atopic dermatitis since 4 weeks of age and severe bronchial asthma, polyvalent allergies and allergic rhinoconjunctivitis presented in January 2024 with erythema on all extremities, generalized xerosis and oozing and received cyclosporine, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, methylprednisolone, levocetirizine, topical therapy and zolpidem.

Lebrikizumab with levocetirizine and topical therapy was started in September 2024, 4 weeks after cyclosporine discontinuation. Baseline EASI was 23.0, DLQI 19.0, peak pruritus NRS 9.0, POEM 21.0 and BSA involvement 80.0%.

After 4 weeks scores were EASI 10.0, DLQI 4.0, POEM 5.0 and peak pruritus NRS 3.0. At week 16 EASI was 3.0, DLQI 2.0, POEM 2.0 and peak pruritus NRS 1.0, with decreased AD severity and amelioration of pruritus, sleep, dyspnea and rhinitis. BSA involvement was reduced to 5.0% and no adverse event was reported.

summary.text: A 24-year-old man with atopic dermatitis since childhood and mild bronchial asthma was hospitalized repeatedly. Prior treatments were external combined treatments with emollients, corticosteroids and antibiotics, and cyclosporine increased from 150 mg/day in 2022 to 300 mg/day in 2024.

Cyclosporine was discontinued and lebrikizumab was started in September 2024, with topical therapy alone continued during the first weeks. Baseline EASI was 36.8, DLQI 17.0, peak pruritus NRS 8.0 and BSA involvement 90.0%.

At week 8 EASI was 16.4, DLQI 10.0 and pruritus NRS 5.0. After 16 weeks EASI was 4.4, DLQI 2.0 and peak pruritus NRS 1.0 with significant clinical reductions. BSA involvement decreased to 10.0% and no adverse event was reported.
